questions.question: The divisor is 10 times the quotient and 5 times the remainder in a division sum. What is the dividend if the remainder is 46?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Remainder** = 46

**Divisor** = 5 × 46 = 230

**Quotient** = 230 ÷ 10 = 23

**Dividend** = (Divisor × Quotient) + Remainder

**Dividend** = (230 × 23) + 46 = 5290 + 46 = 5336

**∴ The correct answer is 5336.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Remainder (R)** = 46

**Divisor (D)** = 5 × Remainder

**Divisor (D)** = 10 × Quotient (Q)

**Formula Used:**

**Dividend** = (**Divisor** × **Quotient**) + **Remainder**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4eff0700c42fead2973351116031a5d3bba1c4cab837582a284d45aca97c3700.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Divisor** = 5 × 46 = 230

⇒ 10 × **Quotient** = 230

⇒ **Quotient** = 230 ÷ 10 = 23

⇒ **Dividend** = (230 × 23) + 46

⇒ **Dividend** = 5290 + 46

⇒ **Dividend** = 5336

**∴ The correct answer is 5336.**

**__Additional Information__**

Division Algorithm

For any two integers a and b, there exist unique integers q and r such that a = bq + r, where 0 ≤ r < b.

Constraint on Remainder

The **remainder** must always be a non-negative integer and must be strictly less than the **divisor**.

Perfect Divisibility

If the **remainder** is 0, the **dividend** is said to be perfectly divisible by the **divisor**.</p

questions.question: If sin θ + cosθ = (1)/(29), find the value of (sintheta+costheta)/(sintheta-costheta)

a sinθ + b cosθ = c 

a sinθ - b cosθ = d

Then we can say that, a2 + b2 = c2 + d2. 

**Calculation:**

a sinθ + b cosθ = c 

a sinθ - b cosθ = d

Then we can say that, a2 + b2 = c2 + d2. 

So 1 + 1 = (1/29)² + d² 

⇒ d² = 2 - 1/841

⇒ 41 /29

(sintheta+costheta)/(sintheta-costheta) = 1/29 × 29/41

⇒ 1/41

**∴ The correct option is 1** [IMAGE: data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAPABAP///wAAACH5BAEKAAAALAAAAAABAAEAAAICRAEAOw==]

questions.question: Mohan completed a certain journey by car. If he covered 30% of the distance at 90 km/h, 45% of the distance at 135 km/h and the remaining distance at 75 km/h. His average speed (in km/h) for the entire journey is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the **Total Distance** be 100 km.

Time taken for first part = 30 ÷ 90 = 1/3 hour.

Time taken for second part = 45 ÷ 135 = 1/3 hour.

Time taken for remaining part (25%) = 25 ÷ 75 = 1/3 hour.

**Total Time** = 1/3 + 1/3 + 1/3 = 1 hour.

**Average Speed** = 100 km ÷ 1 hr = 100 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 100 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance₁ = 30%, Speed₁ = 90 km/h

Distance₂ = 45%, Speed₂ = 135 km/h

Distance₃ = 100% − (30% + 45%) = 25%, Speed₃ = 75 km/h

**Formula Used:**

**Average Speed** = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cad472716cf3948fd7719738ab6df882e8f492d556c087acb2527182dd141cd3.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let total distance be D.

⇒ Total Time (T) = (0.3D ÷ 90) + (0.45D ÷ 135) + (0.25D ÷ 75)

⇒ T = (D ÷ 300) + (D ÷ 300) + (D ÷ 300)

⇒ T = 3D ÷ 300

⇒ T = D ÷ 100

⇒ **Average Speed** = D ÷ (D ÷ 100)

⇒ **Average Speed** = (D × 100) ÷ D

⇒ **Average Speed** = 100 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 100 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Equal Distances

If a journey is divided into 'n' equal distances with speeds v₁, v₂, ..., vₙ, then Average Speed is the **Harmonic Mean** of the speeds.

Average Speed for Two Equal Halves

When two equal distances are covered at speeds 'a' and 'b', Average Speed = (2 × a × b) ÷ (a + b).

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from **km/h to m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert from **m/s to km/h**, multiply by 18/5.</p

A contractor employed 69 workers to complete a work in 20 days. How many more workers he should employ to complete the work in 12 days?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the constant work rule: M₁ × D₁ = M₂ × D₂

69 × 20 = M₂ × 12

Total workers required (M₂) = 1380 ÷ 12 = 115

Additional workers needed = 115 − 69 = 46

**∴ The correct answer is 46 workers.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial number of workers (M₁) = 69

Initial number of days (D₁) = 20

Target number of days (D₂) = 12

**Formula Used:**

Since the total work remains constant, we use the formula: M₁ × D₁ = M₂ × D₂

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total work in man-days = 69 × 20

⇒ Total work = 1380 units

⇒ Let M₂ be the total number of workers required to complete the work in 12 days.

⇒ M₂ × 12 = 1380

⇒ M₂ = 1380 ÷ 12

⇒ M₂ = 115 workers

⇒ The contractor already has 69 workers.

⇒ Number of more workers needed = Total required workers − Initial workers

⇒ Number of more workers = 115 − 69

⇒ Number of more workers = 46

**∴ The correct answer is 46 workers.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

MDH Rule (Chain Rule)

The generalized formula for man-days calculations is (M₁ × D₁ × H₁) ÷ W₁ = (M₂ × D₂ × H₂) ÷ W₂, where M = Men, D = Days, H = Hours, and W = Work.

Time and Efficiency Relationship

Time taken to complete a specific task is inversely proportional to the efficiency or the number of workers. More workers mean fewer days required.

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in direct proportion to the amount of total work completed by the individual, or in the ratio of their efficiencies if everyone works for an equal number of days.
</p
